form.2. SHORT COURSE DESCRIPTION: This course examines modern AI-native software development, where developers collaborate with increasingly capable coding agents. It covers how to define intent, provide effective context, structure development workflows, and coordinate AI tools. Students gain practical experience designing and evaluating agent-assisted software development processes.
form.3. TOPICS / CONTENT AREAS:
Treatment of this list: starting hypotheses — may add/drop/reorder with justification
A. AI-Native Development: AI-assisted coding, coding agents, developer workflows

B. Agentic Software Engineering: MCP, agent skills, tool use, context engineering

C. Specification & Planning: spec-driven development, requirements to executable specifications

D. Software Development Workflows: loop engineering, iterative development, software factories

E. Engineering Practice: automated testing, evaluation, deployment, reliability

F. Practical Development: hands-on coding, projects, emerging developer tools
form.4. COURSE INTENT:
Central question the course answers: How can software developers effectively
design and operate development workflows in which humans and AI agents
collaboratively build reliable software?

Pedagogical emphasis: Practical, workflow-oriented understanding through
hands-on development and experimentation.

This course should NOT become:
- A general introduction to AI or machine learning
- A traditional programming course
- A purely theoretical treatment of large language models
form.5. TARGET STUDENTS:
Programmes: B.Tech. CSE
Year: 3rd/4th year
Assumed background: Strong programming and software development fundamentals;
familiarity with advanced programming and basic software engineering concepts.
form.11. LAB / PRACTICAL COMPONENT:
Lab required: Yes — hands-on coding and development activities

Available infrastructure: Student development machines, access to
AI coding tools/APIs, software development environments, and TA support.
form.12. ASSESSMENT PREFERENCES:
Preferred components: Practical assignments, hands-on coding exercises,
project-based evaluation, and a final project.

Components to avoid: none

Rationale: Assessment should emphasize the ability to apply modern
AI-assisted development practices rather than primarily testing theory.

narrative.course_description: This course examines modern AI-native software development, where developers collaborate with increasingly capable coding agents. It covers how to define intent, provide effective context, structure development workflows, and coordinate AI tools. Students gain practical experience designing and evaluating agent-assisted software development processes. Targeted at third and fourth-year Bachelor of Technology students, the course matters because it prepares engineers for emerging paradigms where autonomous tools integrate directly into the software lifecycle. Upon completion, students will be able to configure AI-assisted coding tools and developer workspaces, translate requirements into executable specifications, deconstruct iterative development loops, evaluate the reliability and performance of AI-generated code, and execute comprehensive AI-native software development projects. The course is taught through a combination of lectures, tutorials, laboratory sessions, and a semester-long project using student development machines and software development environments.
narrative.sequencing_rationale: The modules progress from foundational tools to advanced orchestration, pipelines, and projects, reflecting the prerequisite knowledge from CSE201 and ensuring students master basic coding environments before tackling autonomous agent loops and capstone systems.
narrative.assessment_rationale: The assessment mix—comprising quizzes, assignments, mid-semester and end-semester examinations, laboratory work, and a project—aligns directly with the course outcomes by combining theoretical evaluation with practical, hands-on implementation and system validation.
narrative.positioning_rationale: Unlike CSE201 which teaches manual programming and testing, CSE701 focusing on repository mining, or AI501 covering machine learning theory, this course specifically targets interactive workflows and engineering practices for autonomous coding agents.
